title: refactor(driver-sql): move the NULL-safe unique pre-flight and the declared-index sync out of sql-driver.ts into sql-driver-schema-sync.ts (#25521 cut 9)

_Requested by **Leehom** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X?thread=cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1XCodTCKnBimkFG3aNs3HsTc)_

Cut 9 of the `sql-driver.ts` split (#24586 ruling A, recorded in `6270097840`). The claim is `6420465502`. Cut 8 measured no next slice, so this cut opens with a fresh seam table (below) and takes the area it prices best that breaks no series limit. The bodies of three protected `SqlDriver` methods move unedited into the existing seam module `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-schema-sync.ts`, through its existing host `SchemaSyncHost`:

- `applyNullSafeUniquePreflight`, the plan-side duplicate pre-flight that clears or blocks a unique index op;
- `syncDeclaredIndexes`, which materializes a table's declared indexes;
- `createNullSafeUniqueIndex`, the raw DDL for an organization-scoped unique's expression key.

The module-level helper `formatDuplicateGroups` moves with them, byte-identical with its docblock. Its only two callers are the pre-flight and the sync, so it stays module-local and unexported, as its docblock requires.

These bodies are the rest of the ADR-0120 tightening machinery. Cut 8 already moved its apply side and put the ADR-0120 D4 anchor paragraph on this module's entry. That paragraph describes the duplicate pre-flight, which now lives in the module the paragraph anchors. No anchor entry changes, there is no `docs/adr/**` edit and no `packages/spec/**` edit, and there is no new gate.

The change is move-only, and the card stays open for later cuts. Branch `claude/project-thread-k34erv` (the platform assigned it to this card thread, as the claim records). One commit, `b2b00ab42`, on `origin/main` `e6dfeb08f`.

**Net line count (the seat's rule).** `sql-driver.ts` goes from 21,334 lines to 20,990: **-344**.

- Out: the three bodies, 354 lines (64 + 258 + 32); `formatDuplicateGroups` with its docblock and the blank line before it, 20 lines; and the `describeMissingIndexColumns` import name, 1 line, because its last reader was the moved sync body.
- In: the three stubs, 29 lines (7 + 13 + 9), and 2 import-comment lines.
- The module grows from 372 to 777 lines.

**Serial with the file's in-flight PRs.** I measured this twice: at start, and again before `pr_create` (41 open PRs). Each time I read every open PR's file list in full. Two touch `packages/drivers/driver-sql/**`, and neither touches `src/`: #26203 changes only `tsconfig.json` and #26198 only `package.json`. No PR touches `sql-driver.ts`, `sql-driver-schema-sync.ts`, `turso-driver.ts` or the driver-sql anchor entries.

### Pricing the eligible methods

A method is eligible to move when it meets every condition below. 191 of the 241 instance methods do.

- Its return type is annotated, or it is not public.
- It has no `getBuilder` site.
- It has no `this.FIELD.delete/insert/update(` site.
- It reads no private or protected static.
- It makes no `super` read and no bare `this` pass.
- It makes no write to `this`.
- It is not `insertOnlyUpsertColumns`.

**The net-line rule.** Each candidate is priced as its stub minus its body. A stub costs 4 lines, plus 2 for each field or getter read and 1 for each method read.

The highest-priced candidates, and why each one stays or moves:

Five `packages/cli` `generate-*.pin.test.ts` files also slice `protected createColumn(` … `switch (type)` out of this file's text. |
| `applyFilterCondition` (Filter helpers) | -357 | **Stays.** ADR-0139 cites `sql-driver.ts#applyFilterCondition`, and a governed `.claude/**` reference names it too. `sql-driver-compile-refusal-seam.test.ts` enumerates `INVALID_FILTER` builders in this file only. |

## Why this area

- **It pays the most of any eligible area.** The cut is -344, and the best eligible single method is -245. No candidate priced above it is free of a pointer that a spec or ADR edit would have to move.
- **It belongs in an existing module and host.** `sql-driver-schema-sync.ts` already holds the apply side of the same mechanism (cut 8's `applyIndexDriftOp`, which calls `syncDeclaredIndexes` and `probeNullSafeUniqueDuplicates`). `SchemaSyncHost` already listed 7 of the 10 members these bodies read.
- **No series limit is touched:**
  - none of the three bodies builds through `getBuilder`;
  - none reads a static;
  - none has a `this.FIELD.delete/insert/update(` site;
  - none uses `super`, a bare `this` or a cast-wrapped `this`;
  - all three are protected, with annotated return types.
- **Subclasses.** `TursoDriver` overrides `probeNullSafeUniqueDuplicates` and calls `super`. The bodies reach it through a late-bound closure, so the override is still the one that runs. No subclass overrides any of the three moved methods.
- **Path readers, screened.** No script, test, doc or ADR names any of the three by `sql-driver.ts#…` path, and none slices their text out of `sql-driver.ts`.
  - ADR-0005, ADR-0120, `packages/cli/src/commands/generate.ts` and `driver-turso/src/remote-transport.ts` name `SqlDriver.syncDeclaredIndexes` in prose. That method is still on the class, with the same docblock, so the prose still holds.
  - The only reader of `formatDuplicateGroups` outside its callers is one `{@link formatDuplicateGroups}` in the docblock of `reclaimBetterSqlite3` in `sql-driver.ts`. See Acceptance notes.
- **What stays on purpose.** `probeNullSafeUniqueDuplicates` stays in the class. Its body reads the module-level `uniqueProbeNotNullClause`, so moving it would drag a second helper, and Turso's override already reaches it through the host.

## The shape (#23050 shape B, as cuts 1-8 apply it)

- Each class method keeps its docblock and signature, byte-identical less `async`. Its body is now one host literal plus `NAME.call(host, ...)`, marked `[#25521 cut 9]`, and it returns the moved function's own promise.
- `knex`, `logger` and `isMysql` go as GETTERS that read the driver at call time. The methods go as closures that call the method on the driver at call time. So a subclass override, an instance spy, or a `knex` or `logger` replaced after construction is still the one the body reaches (see the probe below).
- Each moved function types its `this` as the Pick of `SchemaSyncHost` over exactly the members it reads. Each stub annotates its literal as the ThisParameterType of the moved function. There is no cast, and no member becomes public.
- `SchemaSyncHost` gains `createHashShadowUniqueIndex`, `createNullSafeUniqueIndex` and `explainUnkeyableTextColumn`, each typed as the class member's indexed access, in the interface's alphabetical order. The other members these bodies read were already there: `knex`, `logger`, `isMysql`, `getExistingIndexNames`, `logDurabilityFailure`, `probeNullSafeUniqueDuplicates` and `resolveTenantField`.
- **Module-level declarations.**
  - The module imports `normalizeDeclaredIndex`, `describeMissingIndexColumns`, `GLOBAL_TENANT` and the type `DeclaredIndexInput` from `schema-drift.ts`, and `isUniqueViolationError` from `@objectstack/types`, the modules that declare them. No `export` was added anywhere.
  - `sql-driver.ts` drops only `describeMissingIndexColumns` from its import, because the moved sync body was its last reader. Everything else it imported is still read there.
  - `index.ts` re-exports nothing from the module, so the published surface does not move.
- **Comments.** The module header gains a `[#25521 cut 9]` paragraph that cites no decision letter. The `sql-driver.ts` import comment names cut 9 in 2 lines.
- **How the move was made.** A script produced it from the source text; nothing was retyped. Each body line is re-indented two columns. No line in the moved bodies starts inside template-literal text, so no line keeps its base indentation.

## ADR anchors

`check:adr-anchors` counts decision-letter citations on the anchored surface: each anchor's `invariant`, plus the full text of each anchored file.

- **Both files are anchored.** `sql-driver.ts` has its ADR-0053 entry, and `sql-driver-schema-sync.ts` has the ADR-0120 entry cut 8 created.
- **The citations move between anchored files.** The moved bodies carry their `ADR-0120 D3` and `ADR-0120 D4` citations from one anchored file to the other, and the new header paragraph cites no letter.
- **The count.** It is **1883 decision-letter citations at base `e6dfeb08f` and at head `b2b00ab42`**, over 90 anchored files at both ends. Both runs exit 0.
- **No entry needs a new home.** The only paragraph that describes a moved body is the ADR-0120 D4 sentence on the duplicate pre-flight, and it already lives on `sql-driver-schema-sync.ts`'s entry. The ADR-0053 paragraph on `sql-driver.ts` describes `formatOutput` and `presentReadValue`, and neither moved.

## Acceptance notes

- **`check:tenant-chokepoint` rule 2 visits a little less.** Rule 2 (the D8 null-arm rule) scans class members of the three driver files, so it no longer visits what moved:
  - one `knex.raw(` site, `createNullSafeUniqueIndex`'s `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX` with its `COALESCE(... '__global__')` key part (`sql-driver.ts` goes from 57 to 56 `.raw(` sites);
  - `syncDeclaredIndexes`' `tenantField` parameter and its `resolveTenantField` binding.

  None of these says `IS NULL` against a tenant column, and none is a `where` arm. The verdict is unchanged, and the gate is not empty (24 bindings, 3 files). This is the same disclosure cuts 5-7 made, and the card already carries the `SCAN_FILES` precondition.
- **A docblock link no longer resolves in its file.** The docblock of `reclaimBetterSqlite3` in `sql-driver.ts` says "Module-local, like {@link formatDuplicateGroups}", and that helper now lives in `sql-driver-schema-sync.ts`. The sentence is still true, because the helper is still module-local. I left the docblock unedited, since the cut is move-only.
- **Proposed next slice: `applyCrossFieldComparison`** (Filter helpers, about -179, reads 6 methods and no field). It would need a new seam module. Before pricing it at dispatch, screen it against `sql-driver-compile-refusal-seam.test.ts` (whether it builds `INVALID_FILTER`) and against `check:tenant-chokepoint` rule 2.

`skip-changeset`: the change is move-only, so nothing a published package ships changes. The `.d.ts` is byte-identical, and the emitted JS runs the same bodies through the host.
